title: Morphometric Protocol for the Objective Assessment of Blastocyst Behavior During Vitrification and Warming Steps
protocol: Turn off the heating plate of the microscope.
Take a snapshot of a blastocyst under a camera-equipped inverted microscope before any treatment.
Note the magnification at which the blastocyst was recorded.
Select only fully expanded day-5 or day-6 blastocysts for cryopreservation with at least a few inner cell mass (ICM) cells and cohesive trophectoderm.
Subject a laser-treated blastocyst to a short laser pulse (0.4 - 0.7 ms) tangentially directed at the zona pellucida, creating a hole ranging from 4.3 to 9.4 µm in diameter.
Allow the blastocyst to fully or partially collapse for 5 min after treatment.
Perform no particular treatment before vitrification for untreated blastocysts with an intact blastocoel.
Use a pithe pipette (diameter 135 µm) to fill equilibration media into the holes of the microdroplet area of a 9-well Petri dish designed for time-lapse microscopy and recording.
Overlay the microdroplet area with 30 µL of equilibration media.
Transfer a laser-treated or intact blastocyst into the equilibration medium in the microdroplet dish for 10 min at room temperature.
Submerge the blastocyst into the equilibration medium to the bottom of the microdroplet area.
Start a 10-min countdown as soon as the blastocyst is transferred to the equilibration medium.
Transfer the microdroplet dish with the blastocyst to a camera-equipped microscope.
Position the microdroplet dish so that the blastocyst is in the center for recording.
Start recording with the microscope recording software.
Note the countdown time at which the recording is started.
Aseptically dispense a 50-µL drop of vitrification solution in a Petri dish 2 min before the countdown ends.
Stop recording when the 10-min countdown ends.
Transfer the blastocyst to vitrification solution for 30 s at room temperature.
Pipette the blastocyst at least once within the vitrification solution.
Load the blastocyst into a vitrification straw.
Seal and plunge the vitrification straw into liquid nitrogen within 80 s after initial exposure to vitrification solution.
Import a recorded video file into video editing software.
Move the timeline slider to 20 seconds.
Note the frame number at this time.
Click the Video tab, then Frame rate....
Under Frame rate conversion, check the Decimate by field and enter the previously noted frame number.
Confirm settings by clicking OK.
Export images from the video as a sequence using JPEG format.
Choose the directory to hold the saved sequence of images.
Open the video analysis software.
Click the Window tab and select Timeline.
Add an image of the blastocyst before the equilibration phase of vitrification.
Select only the Area data point in the Select Data Points window.
Position the Quick Selection Tool inside the blastocyst to touch its edge.
Outline the blastocyst’s outer edge using the Quick Selection Tool, excluding the zona pellucida.
Record the selected area in the Measurement Log.
Deselect all selections by right-clicking on the image and choosing Deselect.
Move the timeline slider to the next image.
Click on the corresponding tile beneath the slider.
Outline the blastocyst in the new image with the Quick Selection Tool.
Repeat the measurement of the outlined area.
Repeat this procedure for all images until all cross-sectional areas are measured and recorded.
Go to the Measurements Log.
Select all measurements under the Area variable.
Export the selected data into a .txt file.
Transfer the data from the .txt file to a spreadsheet editor.
Use the first cross-sectional area value as reference value 1.
Express all other values as fractions of reference value 1.
Create a new variable named Area_r and paste the transformed area values under it, excluding the reference value.
Next to the Area_r variable, create a Time variable.
Add the first time value which represents the time from when the blastocyst was exposed to the equilibration solution until recording started.
Calculate each consecutive time value by adding 20 seconds to the previous time value.
Prepare media for warming a day before.
Dispense three 150-µL drops of recovery medium in a 4-well dish.
Dispense recovery medium in a microdroplet 9-well dish designed for time-lapse microscopy and recording.
Cover the recovery medium with paraffin oil.
Preincubate the covered medium at 37 °C with 6% CO2 and 5% O2.
Fill holes in the 9-well dish using a pipette for oocyte denudation to avoid air bubbles.
Overlay the microdroplet area with 30 µL of recovery medium.
Dispense 500 µL of thawing solution (TS) in a single well of a 4-well dish.
Allow the TS to warm to 37 °C in an incubator without CO2.
At room temperature, dispense one 50-µL drop of dilution solution and two 50-µL drops of washing solution in a sterile Petri dish.
Cover the DS and WS drops with paraffin oil.
Lift the straw with forceps, just enough to expose the colored handling rod.
Cut the straw at the height of the colored handling rod using a self-adjusting wire stripper.
Extract the handling rod and immediately plunge it into the 37 °C TS.
Gently swirl the handling rod to detach the blastocyst and leave it in TS for 1 min.
Transfer the blastocyst consecutively to DS, WS1, and WS2 for 4 min each at room temperature.
Wash the blastocyst in recovery medium by gently pipetting it in all three drops.
Transfer the blastocyst to a 4-well dish with recovery medium.
Place the 9-well dish under a time-lapse camera in an incubator (37 °C, 6% CO2, and 5% O2).
Run time-lapse recording software.
Choose a recording camera.
Press the Live mode button.
Enlarge the image by placing the mouse cursor on it and using the scroll button.
Move the cursor to place the well with the blastocyst in the middle of the screen.
Use the up-down green arrows to focus the recording plane of the blastocyst.
Set the light intensity.
Click the Microscope parameters button to set the Exposure time and Gamma.
Press Close live mode.
Press the Start project button and enter the project data.
Select the culture dish type (3 x 3 or 4 x 4).
Uncheck all positions except the one to be recorded.
Set the capture timing to take a picture every 5 min.
Start recording by pressing the Approve button.
Record at least 150 min.
Stop recording by pressing the Stop project button.
Go to the project folder and locate recorded images that are roughly 80 KB in size.
Create another folder and transfer these images into it.
Rename the images in numbers according to the time created.
Import them into the video editing software as an image sequence.
Go to Video tab → Filter → Add and select Null transform filter.
Click the Cropping button on the right side and crop the image, leaving visible only the field with the recorded blastocyst.
Confirm with OK and again with OK.
Click File → Export → Image sequence.
Choose JPEG as the output format.
Set the directory to hold the saved sequence of images.
Click OK.
Run the Analyzer of the time-lapse recording software.
Open the project with the recorded blastocyst.
Click the Analyze button on the field with the recorded blastocyst.
Click on the Measurement button in the new Analyze window.
Measure the width of the whole image using the measurement tool.
Right-click on the image and save it.
Check the image’s width in pixels in the properties.
Divide the image’s actual width by its width in pixels to calculate the actual length of a single pixel.
Run the video analysis software.
Click the Window tab and select Timeline.
In the Timeline pane, click on the film strip sign and choose Add Media... to add the image sequence.
Add the image sequence of the post-warm re-expanding blastocyst.
Click Image → Analysis → Set Measurement Scale → Custom in the menu.
For Pixel length, enter 1.
For Logical length, enter the previously calculated actual length of a pixel.
For Logical units, enter μm.
Save the preset.
Measure the blastocyst’s cross-sectional areas using the imported image sequence.
Set units for the measured cross-sectional areas as µm².
Transfer the recorded blastocyst’s cross-sectional area data from the .txt file to a spreadsheet editor.
Create a Time variable next to the Area variable in the spreadsheet.
Enter 0 minutes as the first time value, representing the onset of the time-lapse recording.
Calculate each subsequent time value by adding 5 minutes to the previous time value.
Import the spreadsheet data into statistical analysis software for creating a line diagram.
Generate a time plot showing changes in blastocyst’s cross-sectional area during the equilibration phase.
